lead.headline: Bitcoin's Sunday rally fades as outflow data piles up
lead.standfirst: Bitcoin climbed to $66,000 on Sunday morning before slipping back towards $64,600, while weekend data showed money still leaving crypto funds and stablecoins.
body: Bitcoin rose to about $66,090 on Kraken between 09:00 and 10:00 UK time on Sunday, extending its rebound from an overnight low near $61,970. It drifted back after 14:00 and traded near $64,640 at 16:30 UK, little changed from the morning.

US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $185.4 million on Friday, their seventh consecutive day of outflows, Decrypt reported. That took November's withdrawals to about $2.1 billion and total fund assets to $94.9 billion, below the $100 billion held through much of October.

Money is also draining from stablecoins. Glassnode analysts said supply fell by $17 billion over the past month, the steepest drop since 2022, and the combined value of USDT and USDC slid to $244 billion, its lowest since September 2025, CoinDesk reported.
The Crypto Fear and Greed Index fell to 10 on Sunday, deep in extreme fear, according to Cointelegraph. XRP touched 89 cents, its weakest since November 2024, CoinDesk said.
Zcash held most of its overnight gains, trading near $902 at 16:30 UK after a high of about $930 before midday. Attention now turns to the weekly close at midnight UK and Monday's ETF figures.

headline: A quiet Sunday afternoon: bitcoin's rally to $66,000 faded back to about $64,600. Weekend data showed a seventh day of ETF outflows and shrinking stablecoin supply.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, afternoon edition. A quiet Sunday. Bitcoin climbed to about sixty-six thousand dollars this morning, then slipped back and is trading near sixty-four thousand six hundred, close to where it was at breakfast. Weekend figures showed US bitcoin funds lost money for a seventh day running on Friday, about two point one billion dollars so far in November, and stablecoin supply is shrinking fast. Zcash is holding near nine hundred dollars. Watch the weekly close at midnight and Monday's fund flows. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin's rebound reaches $66,000, then fades
stories.why: Since the morning edition bitcoin rose from about $64,470 to a high near $66,090 on Kraken between 09:00 and 10:00 UK, held around $65,300 to $65,500 into early afternoon, then fell to about $64,430 after 14:00 and traded near $64,640 at 16:30 UK. Cointelegraph, citing CoinGecko, put the overnight low at $62,081 and the weekly fall at nearly 15%.
stories.caveat: Exchanges printed slightly different figures: the overnight low was about $61,970 on Kraken and $62,081 on CoinGecko.

note.read: Failing to hold $65,500 suggests buyers are cautious after the flush; the overnight low is now the line traders will watch.
note.alt: Sunday trade is thin, and the drift back may be routine profit-taking rather than renewed selling.
note.change: A weekly close above about $65,500 would ease the pressure; a return below $62,000 would point to a test of $60,000.

stories.title: Bitcoin ETF outflows hit seven straight days
stories.why: Decrypt reported $185.4 million of outflows on Friday, the seventh straight trading day, about $2.1 billion so far in November and total assets of $94.9 billion. Cointelegraph said BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust has now had outflows for 11 sessions in a row.
stories.caveat: Weekly totals differ by tracker: about $829 million for the week (Decrypt) against $1.07 billion (Cointelegraph).

note.read: Steady withdrawals from the largest fund suggest institutional buyers are stepping back rather than buying the dip.
note.alt: Some outflows may be hedge funds unwinding trades that pair ETF holdings with futures, which says less about long-term demand.
note.change: A day of net inflows on Monday or Tuesday, especially into BlackRock's fund, would break the pattern.

stories.title: Stablecoin supply shrinks $17 billion in a month
stories.why: Glassnode analysts said stablecoin supply fell $17 billion over the past month, the steepest drop since 2022, and the combined value of USDT and USDC fell to $244 billion from about $270 billion in early May, CoinDesk reported. Fewer stablecoins means less ready cash on exchanges to buy crypto.

note.read: Shrinking stablecoin supply alongside ETF outflows points to money leaving crypto altogether, not just moving between coins.
note.alt: Some of the fall may reflect redemptions for other uses, such as payments or moves into tokenised Treasury funds, rather than sellers exiting.
note.change: Stablecoin supply growing again for several weeks would suggest fresh money returning.

stories.title: Zcash holds near $900
stories.why: Zcash kept its overnight rebound, reaching about $930 on Kraken before midday, dipping to about $876 after 14:00 with bitcoin, and trading near $902 at 16:30 UK, slightly above the morning's $894. No new Zcash news found.

stories.title: Crypto sentiment index falls to 10, extreme fear
stories.why: The Crypto Fear and Greed Index fell to 10 on Sunday from 13 on Saturday and 20 on Friday, Cointelegraph reported, citing Alternative.me. Total crypto market value fell about 4% in 24 hours to $2.26 trillion.

stories.title: XRP falls to 89 cents, its lowest since November 2024
stories.why: CoinDesk reported XRP down 36% this quarter, with US XRP ETFs losing $19.13 million last week, their largest weekly outflow since March, according to SoSoValue. A sign the sell-off is broad, not bitcoin-specific.

explained.title: Why stablecoin supply matters
body: Stablecoins such as USDT and USDC are tokens pegged to the dollar. Traders hold them on exchanges as ready cash, so the total supply is a rough gauge of how much money is sitting inside crypto waiting to be used.
When supply grows, new dollars are coming in. When it shrinks, holders are redeeming tokens for real dollars and taking them out, which leaves less buying power for bitcoin and other coins.

investigating: Was $62,000 the low of this leg? Evidence: the weekly close tonight and whether bitcoin holds above $62,000 into Monday's US session.
Will ETF outflows run to an eighth day? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue figures for Monday 16 November.
